audit.whatIsWrong: Two fields state that Zac has 'no percent-HP damage'. Unstable Matter (W) explicitly deals a percentage of the target's maximum health as magic damage, on a flat 5 s cooldown, and his passive is flagged percent-health as well. The page also calls that same W a slow — it has no slow; the slows are on Stretching Strikes (Q) and Let's Bounce! (R).
audit.why: This is the one claim on the page that could actively lose the game: Swain's whole plan here is stacking maximum health off Soul Fragments, and the reader is told the enemy has nothing that punishes it. He has exactly that, every five seconds.
audit.corrected: whys[6] and late now name Unstable Matter as max-health damage on a 5 s cooldown; mid stops calling the W a slow.
sources: enemyKit W text and percentHealth flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 and Level 6 sit at 'Skill' although their whys say your leads compound and that Demonic Ascension is the equalizer his kit 'cannot kill a healing Swain' through. Packet chart gives Swain every row from Level 2 onward.
audit.why: Two rows contradicted their own explanations in a 55.83% matchup — the strongest lane in this slice.
audit.corrected: Rows 3 and 4 to Swain at 7/10; win[] and phases[].side proposed as pairs.

audit.why: Four spikes present: Level 2 root, Level 6 drain, first item, and his Let's Bounce! window. Elastic Slingshot at 21/18/15/12/9 s is the cooldown the page is built on tracking; it only lacked a number.
audit.corrected: Rank-1 21 s added to the Elastic Slingshot Don't.

audit.why: The blob-reabsorption sustain is already covered across whys[2], whys[3], early and the itemization anti-heal line, which answers the flagged needs-antiheal interaction. Cell Division's revive on fatal damage is not described anywhere, but the page never tells the reader to expect a clean kill, so no negative was added.

edits.before: Zac has no true damage, no percent-HP, and no untargetable frame — your fragment-stacked max HP and permanent R healing make you a drain tank he simply cannot kill in a 1v1.
edits.after: Unstable Matter (W) burns a share of your max HP every 5 s, so fragment stacking alone is not armour — but with R healing on top he still cannot close the 1v1.

edits.before: Zac scales reasonably as an engage tank but Swain scales into an unkillable drain monster — his ult does not outpace your R sustain, and his kit has no percent-HP damage, no true damage, and no untargetable window to dodge your Demonflare nova. In teamfights, drop W in the cluster before he R-engages to root him on arrival, then chain E and activate Demonic Ascension for a teamfight drain that heals off everyone he dragged in. The only late danger is getting caught flat-footed by a full Let's Bounce chain without R available — track its cooldown and never engage in a skirmish without your R ready to ride through his knock-ups.
edits.after: Zac scales reasonably as an engage tank but Swain scales into an unkillable drain monster — his ult does not outpace your R sustain, and his only max-health damage is Unstable Matter every 5 s, with no untargetable window to dodge your Demonflare nova. In teamfights, drop W in the cluster before he R-engages to root him on arrival, then chain E and activate Demonic Ascension for a drain that heals off everyone he dragged in. The late danger is a full Let's Bounce! chain caught without R — it is down 120 s at rank 1, so track it and never skirmish without your own R ready.

edits.before: Once your root-pull pattern is established and your R is online, Zac has almost no answer to your sustained pressure. His R is threatening if he can chain knock-ups and land all four bounces on you, but Demonic Ascension makes that window survivable — pop it the moment he initiates his bounce chain and drain through the displacement. Between fights, look for E on his E telegraph: he cannot dodge your hand in mid-air when his sling is committed. Keep the wave frozen near your side of lane so he must walk into your W range to contest, and punish every overextension with a full W-E-pull-Q rotation. His W slow is minor; your slow into root combo is far more punishing to the trade pattern.
edits.after: Once your root-pull pattern is established and your R is online, Zac has almost no answer to your sustained pressure. His R is threatening if he can chain knock-ups and land all four bounces on you, but Demonic Ascension makes that window survivable — pop it the moment he initiates his bounce chain and drain through the displacement. Between fights, look for E on his E telegraph: he cannot dodge your hand in mid-air when his sling is committed. Keep the wave frozen near your side so he must walk into your W range to contest, and punish every overextension with a full W-E-pull-Q rotation. His W chips your max health every 5 s — do not stand in it while you drain.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Elastic Slingshot is down 21 s at rank 1 — punish the whole window.

notes: The claim that Zac has no percent-health damage appeared twice and is wrong: Unstable Matter (W) deals a share of maximum health on a flat 5 s cooldown, which directly punishes the Soul Fragment max-HP stacking this page recommends. The W was also described as a slow; it is not. Mirror audit on the Zac side was consulted — its Nevermove (E) / Vision of Empire (W) assignments match what I used here, and its flagged suspectName is a false positive, as is 'Let's Bounce' vs 'Let's Bounce!' in the late text. Chart rows 3 and 4 flipped to packet.levelChart as matched pairs.
